sentences.zh: 自詩書稱三代「戎狄是膺，荊荼是徵」，太史公曰：齊桓越燕伐山戎，武靈王以區區趙服單于，秦繆用百里霸西戎，吳楚之君以諸侯役百越。

translations.literal: Since the Odes and Documents praise the Three Dynasties for 'repelling the Rong and Di, chastising Jing and Chu,' the Grand Historian said: Duke Huan of Qi crossed Yan to attack the Shanrong; King Wuling of Zhao, though ruling a small state, made the Chanyu submit; Duke Mu of Qin, with Baili Xi, became hegemon over the Western Rong; and the rulers of Wu and Chu used the feudal lords to make the Hundred Yue submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes and Documents praise the Three Dynasties for "repelling the Rong and Di and chastising Jing and Chu." As the Grand Historian said: Duke Huan of Qi crossed through Yan to attack the Shanrong; King Wuling of Zhao, though ruling only a small state, brought the Chanyu to submission; Duke Mu of Qin used Baili Xi to become hegemon over the Western Rong; and the rulers of Wu and Chu employed the feudal lords to subdue the Hundred Yue.

sentences.zh: 況乃以中國一統，明天子在上，兼文武，席卷四海，內輯億萬之眾，豈以晏然不為邊境征伐哉！

translations.literal: How much more so when China was unified, the enlightened Son of Heaven sat above, combining civil and military power, sweeping across the four seas, and gathering millions within—how could he remain at ease and not conduct border campaigns?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when China was unified, with the enlightened Son of Heaven above, combining civil and military power, sweeping across the four seas, and gathering millions within—how could he remain complacent and fail to wage border campaigns?

sentences.zh: 自是後，遂出師北討彊胡，南誅勁越，將卒以次封矣。

translations.literal: After this, they sent armies north to attack the strong Hu and south to suppress the strong Yue, and generals and soldiers were enfeoffed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, armies went out northward to campaign against the powerful Hu and southward to punish the formidable Yue, and generals and soldiers received enfeoffments one after another.

cells.content: 以小月氏若苴王將眾降侯。
cells.literal: The Little Yuezhi Ruju king led his people in surrender and was made a marquis.
cells.idiomatic: The Little Yuezhi Ruju king led his people in surrender and was made a marquis.

cells.content: 三。四年十一月丁卯，侯稽谷姑。元年。
cells.literal: Three. Fourth year eleventh month dingmao, Marquis Ji Gu Gu first year.
cells.idiomatic: Three. Fourth year, eleventh month, dingmao day: first year of Marquis Jigugu.

cells.content: 太初元年，侯稽谷姑薨，無後，國除。
cells.literal: The first year of Taichu, Marquis Ji Gu Gu died without heirs, and the state was abolished.
cells.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu, Marquis Jigugu died without heirs, and the state was abolished.

cells.content: 浩。
cells.literal: Hao
cells.idiomatic: Hao

cells.content: 以故中郎將將兵捕得車師王功侯。
cells.literal: As former Palace Attendant General led troops captured Cheshi king with merit, Marquis.
cells.idiomatic: As a former Palace Attendant General, he led troops, captured the King of Cheshi, and was made a marquis for his merit.

cells.content: 一。四年正月甲申，侯王恢元年。四年四月，侯恢坐使酒泉矯制害，當死，贖，國除。封凡三月。
cells.literal: One. Fourth year, first month, jiashen day: first year of Marquis Wang Hui. Fourth year, fourth month: Marquis Hui was convicted of, as envoy to Jiuquan, forging imperial orders to cause harm; he was liable for death, ransomed the offense, and the state was abolished. The enfeoffment lasted three months.
cells.idiomatic: One. Fourth year, first month, jiashen day: first year of Marquis Wang Hui. Fourth year, fourth month: Marquis Hui was convicted of forging imperial orders to cause harm while serving as envoy to Jiuquan; he was liable for death, ransomed the offense, and the marquisate was abolished. The enfeoffment lasted three months.

cells.content: 瓡讘。
cells.literal: Li Zan
cells.idiomatic: Li Zan

cells.content: 以小月氏王將眾千騎降侯。
cells.literal: The Little Yuezhi king led one thousand cavalry in surrender and was made a marquis.
cells.idiomatic: As king of the Little Yuezhi, he led a thousand cavalry in surrender and was made a marquis.

cells.content: 二。四年正月乙酉，侯扜者。元年。一。六年，侯勝元年。
cells.literal: Two. Fourth year first month yiyou, Marquis Ya Zhe first year. One. Sixth year, Marquis Sheng first year.
cells.idiomatic: Two. Fourth year first month yiyou day, Marquis Ya Zhe began his tenure. One. Sixth year, Marquis Sheng began his tenure.

cells.content: 四
cells.literal: Four
cells.idiomatic: Four

cells.content: 幾。
cells.literal: Ji
cells.idiomatic: Ji

cells.content: 以朝鮮王子漢兵圍朝鮮降侯。
cells.literal: A prince of Chaoxian surrendered when Han troops surrounded Chaoxian and was made a marquis.
cells.idiomatic: A prince of Chaoxian surrendered when Han troops surrounded Chaoxian and was made a marquis.

cells.content: 二。四年三月癸未，侯張阍。。歸義元年。六年，侯張阍使朝鮮，謀反，死，國除。
cells.literal: Two. Fourth year third month guiwei, Marquis Zhang Hun first year. Gui Yi. Sixth year, Marquis Zhang Hun sent to Chaoxian, plotted rebellion, died, the state was abolished.
cells.idiomatic: Two. Fourth year third month guiwei day, Marquis Zhang Hun began his tenure. Gui Yi. Sixth year, Marquis Zhang Hun sent to Chaoxian, plotted rebellion, died, the state was abolished.

cells.content: 涅陽。
cells.literal: Nie Yang
cells.idiomatic: Nie Yang

cells.content: 以朝鮮相路人，漢兵至，首先降，道死，其子侯。
cells.literal: Lu Ren, Prime Minister of Chaoxian, was the first to surrender when Han troops arrived. He died on the road, and his son was made a marquis.
cells.idiomatic: Lu Ren, Prime Minister of Chaoxian, was the first to surrender when Han troops arrived. He died on the road, and his son was made a marquis.

cells.content: 三。四年三月壬寅，康侯子最元年。
cells.literal: Three. Fourth year third month renyin, Marquis Kang Zi Zui first year.
cells.idiomatic: Three. Fourth year third month renyin day, Marquis Kang Zi Zui began his tenure.

cells.content: 二。太初二年，侯最死，無後，國除。
cells.literal: Two. The second year of Taichu, Marquis Zui died without heirs, and the state was abolished.
cells.idiomatic: Two. In the second year of Taichu, Marquis Zui died without heirs, and the state was abolished.

translations.literal: Above: the Grand Historian's original table.
translations.idiomatic: The preceding is the Grand Historian's original table.

cells.content: 當塗。
cells.literal: Dangtu.
cells.idiomatic: Dangtu.

cells.content: 魏不害，以圉守尉捕淮陽反者公孫勇等侯。
cells.literal: Wei Buhai, as defense commandant of Yu, captured Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels and was made marquis.
cells.idiomatic: Wei Buhai was made marquis for capturing Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels while serving as defense commandant of Yu.

cells.content: 蒲。
cells.literal: Pu.
cells.idiomatic: Pu.

cells.content: 蘇昌，以圉尉史捕淮陽反者公孫勇等侯。
cells.literal: Su Chang, as clerk to the commandant of Yu, captured Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels and was made marquis.
cells.idiomatic: Su Chang was made marquis for capturing Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels while serving as clerk to the commandant of Yu.

cells.content: 潦陽。
cells.literal: Liaoyang.
cells.idiomatic: Liaoyang.

cells.content: 江德，以園廄嗇夫共捕淮陽反者公孫勇等侯。
cells.literal: Jiang De, as steward of the park stables, joined in capturing Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels and was made marquis.
cells.idiomatic: Jiang De was made marquis for joining in the capture of Gongsun Yong and the other Huaiyang rebels while serving as steward of the park stables.

cells.content: 富民。
cells.literal: Fumin.
cells.idiomatic: Fumin.

cells.content: 田千秋，家在長陵。以故高廟寢郎上書諫孝武曰：「子弄父兵，罪當笞。父子之怒，自古有之。蚩尤畔父，黃帝涉江」。上書至意，拜為大鴻臚。征和四年為丞相，封三千戶。至昭帝時病死，子順代立，為虎牙將軍，擊匈奴，不至質，誅死，國除。
cells.literal: Tian Qianqiu, whose family was in Changling. As a former chamber gentleman of the Gao Temple, he submitted a memorial admonishing Emperor Xiaowu, saying, "When a son plays with his father's weapons, the offense should be punished with flogging. Anger between father and son has existed since antiquity. Chiyou rebelled against his father, and the Yellow Emperor crossed the river." When the memorial arrived and its meaning was appreciated, he was appointed Grand Herald. In the fourth year of Zhenghe he became Chancellor and was enfeoffed with three thousand households. By Emperor Zhao's time he died of illness; his son Shun succeeded, became General of Tiger Teeth, attacked the Xiongnu, failed to reach the rendezvous, was executed, and the state was abolished.
cells.idiomatic: Tian Qianqiu, whose family was in Changling, had formerly served as a chamber gentleman at the Gao Temple. He submitted a memorial admonishing Emperor Xiaowu: "When a son plays with his father's weapons, he deserves flogging. Anger between father and son has existed since antiquity. Chiyou rebelled against his father, and the Yellow Emperor crossed the river." The memorial was well received, and he was appointed Grand Herald. In the fourth year of Zhenghe he became Chancellor and was enfeoffed with three thousand households. In Emperor Zhao's time he died of illness. His son Shun succeeded him, became General of Tiger Teeth, attacked the Xiongnu, failed to reach the rendezvous, was executed, and the state was abolished.

translations.literal: Above are the names of the fiefs enfeoffed under Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The above lists the fiefs enfeoffed under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 後進好事儒者褚先生曰：太史公記事盡於孝武之事，故復修記孝昭以來功臣侯者，編於左方，令後好事者得覽觀成敗長短絕世之適，得以自戒焉。

translations.literal: Mr. Chu, a later scholar fond of such matters, said: The Grand Historian's account ends with the affairs of Emperor Wu, so he compiled again the records of meritorious ministers and marquises from Emperor Zhao onward, placing them on the left, so that later scholars may look on the successes and failures, the long and short of these severed lineages, and use them to warn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Chu, a later scholar fond of such matters, said: The Grand Historian's account ends with the affairs of Emperor Wu. Therefore, he again compiled records of meritorious ministers and marquises from Emperor Zhao onward and placed them on the left. Later scholars may examine the successes and failures, the long and short spans of these severed lineages, and use them as warnings.

sentences.zh: 當世之君子，行權合變，度時施宜，希世用事，以建功有土封侯，立名當世，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: The gentlemen of the present age adapt to changing circumstances, gauge the time, and act as the moment requires; they win merit, receive land, and are enfeoffed as marquises, making a name in their own day. Is this not splendid!
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of the present age adapt to circumstance, respond to change, judge the times, and act as conditions require; they achieve merit, receive territory, are enfeoffed as marquises, and establish their names in their own day. Is this not magnificent!

sentences.zh: 觀其持滿守成之道，皆不謙讓，驕蹇爭權，喜揚聲譽，知進不知退，終以殺身滅國。

translations.literal: Observe their way of preserving what they had won: all were unyielding and contentious, arrogant in their struggle for power, fond of proclaiming their reputations, knowing only how to advance and not how to retreat, and in the end they lost their lives and destroyed their states.
translations.idiomatic: Yet observe how they preserve fullness and guard achievement: they are never modest or yielding, but haughty, contentious, eager to fight for power, fond of broadcasting their reputations, and know only how to advance, not how to withdraw. In the end, they lose their lives and destroy their states.

sentences.zh: 以三得之，及身失之，不能傳功於後世，令恩德流子孫，豈不悲哉！

translations.literal: Having obtained it in three generations, they lost it in their own person and could not pass their merit on to later generations or let their beneficence flow to descendants. Is this not sad!
translations.idiomatic: What they gained over three generations they lost in their own persons, unable to transmit their merit to later ages or let their beneficence flow down to their descendants. Is this not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 夫龍雒侯曾為前將軍，世俗順善，厚重謹信，不與政事，退讓愛人。

translations.literal: Marquis Longluo once served as Forward General. He was mild and congenial, grave, careful, and trustworthy. He took no part in politics, was retiring and yielding, and loved people.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Longluo once served as Forward General. He was gentle and good-natured, grave, careful, and trustworthy; he did not involve himself in political affairs, but withdrew, yielded, and loved others.

translations.literal: His ancestors arose in the age of Jin's six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears rose in the age of Jin's six ministers.

sentences.zh: 有土君國以來，為王侯，子孫相承不絕，歷年經世，以至于今，凡百餘歲，豈可與功臣及身失之者同日而語之哉？

translations.literal: Since they first acquired territory and ruled as kings and marquises, their descendants have inherited without interruption through the years and generations, and now for more than a hundred years. How can they be spoken of in the same breath as meritorious ministers who lost everything in their own persons?
translations.idiomatic: From the time they first held territory and ruled states as kings and marquises, their descendants have inherited without interruption across years and generations down to the present, for more than a hundred years in all. How can they be spoken of in the same breath as meritorious ministers who lost everything within their own lifetimes?

translations.literal: Alas, let later generations take warning from this!
translations.idiomatic: How sad! Let later generations take warning from it.

cells.content: 博陸
cells.literal: Bo Lu
cells.idiomatic: Bo Lu

cells.content: 霍光，家在平陽。以兄驃騎將軍故貴。前事武帝，覺捕得侍中謀反者馬何羅等功侯，三千戶。中輔幼主昭帝，為大將軍。謹信，用事擅治，尊為大司馬，益封邑萬戶。後事宣帝。歷事三主，天下信鄉之，益封二萬戶。子禹代立，謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Huo Guang, whose family was in Pingyang, rose in rank because his elder brother was the Cavalry General. He first served Emperor Wu and, after uncovering and arresting the conspirators Ma Heluo and others, was enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. He then assisted the young Emperor Zhao and became Grand General. Careful and trustworthy, he managed affairs and held power, was honored as Grand Marshal, and had his fief increased by 10,000 households. Later he served Emperor Xuan. He served three rulers, and the empire trusted and admired him, so his enfeoffment was increased by 20,000 households. His son Yu succeeded him, plotted rebellion, and the clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.content: 秺。
cells.literal: Du
cells.idiomatic: Du

cells.content: 金翁叔名日磾，以匈奴休屠王太子從渾邪王將眾五萬，降漢歸義，侍中，事武帝，覺捕侍中謀反者馬何羅等功侯，三千戶。中事昭帝，謹厚，益封三千戶。子弘代立，為奉車都尉，事宣帝。
cells.literal: Jin Wengshu, whose personal name was Ridi, was the crown prince of the Xiongnu Xiutu king. He followed the Hunye king, led 50,000 men, surrendered to Han, and returned to righteousness. He served as a Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu and, after uncovering and arresting the conspirators Ma Heluo and others, was enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. He later served Emperor Zhao, remained careful and prudent, and had his enfeoffment increased by 3,000 households. His son Hong succeeded him and became Carriage Escort Colonel under Emperor Xuan.
cells.idiomatic: Jin Wengshu, whose personal name was Ridi, was the crown prince of the Xiongnu Xiutu king. cells.content: 安陽。
cells.literal: An Yang
cells.idiomatic: Anyang

cells.content: 上官桀，家在隴西。以善騎射從軍。稍貴，事武帝，為左將軍。覺捕斬侍中謀反者馬何羅弟重合侯通功侯，三千戶。中事昭帝，與大將軍霍光爭權，因以謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Shangguan Jie, whose family was in Longxi, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and followed the army. As he rose in rank, he served Emperor Wu and became Left General. After uncovering and beheading Ma Heluo and his younger brother, Marquis Tong of Chonghe, who had plotted rebellion, he was enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. Later, while serving Emperor Zhao, he contended with Grand General Huo Guang for power and therefore plotted rebellion; his clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.content: 桑樂。
cells.literal: Sang Le
cells.idiomatic: Sang Le

cells.content: 上官安。以父桀為將軍故貴，侍中，事昭帝。安女為昭帝夫人，立為皇后故侯，三千戶。驕蹇，與大將軍霍光爭權，因以父子謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Shangguan An, because his father Jie had been a general, was himself treated as noble and served as a Palace Attendant under Emperor Zhao. An's daughter became Emperor Zhao's consort and was installed as Empress, and he was therefore enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. Arrogant and contentious, he vied with Grand General Huo Guang for power, and so father and son plotted rebellion; their clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.content: 富平。
cells.literal: Fu Ping
cells.idiomatic: Fu Ping

cells.content: 張安世，家在杜陵。以故御史大夫張湯子武帝時給事尚書，為尚書令。事昭帝，謹厚習事，為光祿勳右將軍。輔政十三年，無適過，侯，三千戶。及事宣帝，代霍光為大司馬，用事，益封萬六千戶。子延壽代立，為太僕，侍中。
cells.literal: Zhang Anshi, whose family was in Duling, was the son of the former Grand Minister of Justice Zhang Tang. During Emperor Wu's reign he served in the Shangshu office and became its Director. Under Emperor Zhao he served diligently and carefully and became Director of the Imperial Clan and Right General. He assisted the government for thirteen years without fault and was enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. Under Emperor Xuan he replaced Huo Guang as Grand Marshal, handled affairs, and had his enfeoffment increased by 16,000 households. His son Yanshou succeeded him and became Grand Servant Treasurer and Palace Attendant.

cells.content: 義陽。
cells.literal: Yi Yang
cells.idiomatic: Yi Yang

cells.content: 傅介子，家在北地。以從軍為郎，為平樂監。昭帝時，刺殺外國王，天子下詔書曰：「平樂監傅介子使外國，殺樓蘭王，以直報怨，不煩師，有功，其以邑千三百戶封介子為義陽侯。」子厲代立，爭財相告，有罪，國除。
cells.literal: Fu Jiezhi, whose family was in Beidi, followed the army and became a Palace Attendant, then Pingle Supervisor. Under Emperor Zhao he assassinated a foreign king, and the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: 'Pingle Supervisor Fu Jiezhi was sent abroad, killed the King of Loulan, and avenged resentment directly without troubling the armies. He has merit, and therefore let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang with a fief of 1,300 households.' His son Li succeeded, but after disputes over property they accused one another, were convicted of crimes, and the state was abolished.

cells.content: 商利。
cells.literal: Shang Li
cells.idiomatic: Shang Li

cells.content: 王山，齊人也。故為丞相史，會騎將軍上官安謀反，山說安與俱入丞相，斬安。山以軍功為侯，三千戶。上書願治民，為代太守。為人所上書言，繫獄當死，會赦，出為庶人，國除。
cells.literal: Wang Shan, a man of Qi, had formerly served as a Chancellor Historian. When he encountered Cavalry General Shangguan An plotting rebellion, Shan persuaded An to enter the Chancellor's office with him and beheaded An. For his military merit Shan was enfeoffed as a marquis with 3,000 households. He memorialized that he wished to govern the people and became Grand Administrator of Dai. Someone then memorialized against him, he was imprisoned and should have died, but an amnesty came, and he was released as a commoner; his state was abolished.

cells.content: 建平。
cells.literal: Jian Ping
cells.idiomatic: Jian Ping

cells.content: 杜延年。以故御史大夫杜周子給事大將軍幕府，發覺謀反者騎將軍上官安等罪，封為侯，邑二千七百戶，拜為太僕。元年，出為西河太守。五鳳三年，入為御史大夫。
cells.literal: Du Yannian, the son of the former Grand Minister of Justice Du Zhou, served in the Grand General's headquarters and uncovered the crimes of Cavalry General Shangguan An and the others who plotted rebellion. He was enfeoffed as a marquis with a fief of 2,700 households and appointed Grand Servant Treasurer. In the first year he went out as Grand Administrator of Xihe. In Wufeng's third year he entered office as Grand Minister of Justice.

cells.content: 弋陽。
cells.literal: Yi Yang
cells.idiomatic: Yi Yang

cells.content: 任宮。以故上林尉捕格謀反者左將軍上官桀，殺之便門，封為侯，二千戶。後為太常，及行衛尉事。節儉謹信，以壽終，傳於子孫。
cells.literal: Ren Gong, as a former Shanglin Guard, captured and subdued the rebel Left General Shangguan Jie, killed him at Bian Gate, and was enfeoffed as a marquis with 2,000 households. Later he became Grand Master of Ceremonies and also handled the affairs of the Commander of the Guards. Frugal, careful, and trustworthy, he ended his life in old age and passed his line down to his descendants.

Frugal, careful, and trustworthy, he ended his life in old age and passed his line down to his descendants.

cells.content: 宜城。
cells.literal: Yi Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Yi Cheng

cells.content: 燕倉。以故大將軍幕府軍吏發謀反者騎將軍上官安罪有功，封侯，邑二千戶。為汝南太守，有能名。
cells.literal: Yan Cang, a former army official in the Grand General's headquarters, uncovered the crimes of Cavalry General Shangguan An, who was plotting rebellion, and was therefore enfeoffed as a marquis with a fief of 2,000 households. He later became Grand Administrator of Runan and earned a reputation for ability.

cells.content: 宜春。
cells.literal: Yi Chun
cells.idiomatic: Yi Chun

cells.content: 王訢，家在齊。本小吏佐史，稍遷至右輔都尉。武帝數幸扶風郡，訢共置辦，拜為右扶風。至孝昭時，代桑弘羊為御史大夫。元鳳三年，代田千秋為丞相，封二千戶。立二年，為人所上書言暴，自殺，不殊。子代立，為屬國都尉。
cells.literal: Wang Xun, whose family was in Qi, began as a low official and assistant historian and was gradually promoted to Right Auxiliary Colonel. When Emperor Wu frequently visited Fufeng commandery, Xun arranged the preparations and was appointed Right Fufeng. Under Emperor Zhao he replaced Sang Hongyang as Grand Minister of Justice. In Yuanfeng's third year he replaced Tian Qianqiu as Chancellor and was enfeoffed with 2,000 households. He held the post for two years, then was denounced as violent, and killed himself, though the details are not clear. His son succeeded him and became Dependent State Colonel.

cells.content: 楊敞，家在華陰。故給事大將軍幕府，稍遷至大司農，為御史大夫。元鳳六年，代王訢為丞相，封二千戶。立二年，病死。子賁代立，十三年病死。子翁君代立，為典屬國。三歲，以季父惲故出惡言，繫獄當死，得免，為庶人，國除。
cells.literal: Yang Chang, whose family was in Huayin, had formerly served in the Grand General's headquarters and was gradually promoted to Grand Agrarian and then Grand Minister of Justice. In Yuanfeng's sixth year he replaced Wang Xun as Chancellor and was enfeoffed with 2,000 households. He held office for two years and died of illness. His son Ben succeeded him and died of illness after thirteen years. His son Wengjun succeeded him and became Superintendent of Dependent States. In the third year, because of evil words spoken about his maternal uncle Yun, he was imprisoned and should have died, but he obtained pardon, became a commoner, and his state was abolished.

cells.content: 陽平。
cells.literal: Yang Ping
cells.idiomatic: Yang Ping

cells.content: 蔡義，家在溫。故師受韓詩，為博士，給事大將軍幕府，為杜城門候。入侍中，授昭帝韓詩，為御史大夫。是時年八十，衰老，常兩人扶持乃能行。然公卿大臣議，以為為人主師，當以為相。以元平元年代楊敞為丞相，封二千戶。病死，絕無後，國除。
cells.literal: Cai Yi, whose family was in Wen, had studied the Han Poetry under a teacher and became a doctorate. He served in the Grand General's headquarters and became Gate Guard of Ducheng. He entered as a Palace Attendant, taught Emperor Zhao the Han Poetry, and became Grand Minister of Justice. By then he was eighty and so old that he needed two men supporting him to walk. Yet the ministers and high officials discussed him and thought that, as a teacher to the ruler, he should become chancellor. In Yuanping's first year he replaced Yang Chang as Chancellor and was enfeoffed with 2,000 households. He died of illness, leaving left no heirs, and his state was abolished.

cells.content: 扶陽。
cells.literal: Fu Yang
cells.idiomatic: Fu Yang

cells.content: 韋賢，家在魯。通詩、禮、尚書，為博士，授魯大儒，入侍中，為昭帝師，遷為光祿大夫，大鴻臚，長信少府。以為人主師，本始三年代蔡義為丞相，封扶陽侯，千八百戶。為丞相五歲，多恩，不習吏事，免相就第，病死。子玄成代立，為太常。坐祠廟騎，奪爵，為關內侯。
cells.literal: Wei Xian, whose family was in Lu, mastered the Odes, the Rites, and the Shangshu, became a doctorate, and taught many great Confucians in Lu. He entered as a Palace Attendant, became Emperor Zhao's teacher, and was promoted to Guanglu Dafu, Grand Honglu, and Changxin Shaofu. Because he was regarded as the ruler's teacher, in Benshi's third year he replaced Cai Yi as Chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang with 1,800 households. He served as Chancellor for five years, was very benevolent, and was not practiced in official affairs. After being dismissed he went to his residence and died of illness. His son Xuancheng succeeded him and became Grand Master of Ceremonies. Convicted over riding a horse at a temple sacrifice, he lost his title and became a marquis within the passes.

cells.literal: Ping Ling
cells.idiomatic: Ping Ling

cells.content: 范明友，家在隴西。以家世習外國事，使護西羌。事昭帝，拜為度遼將軍，擊烏桓功侯，二千戶。取霍光女為妻。地節四年，與諸霍子禹等謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Fan Mingyou, whose family was in Longxi, had for generations practiced foreign affairs and was sent to guard the Western Qiang. Under Emperor Zhao he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Liao and, for his merits in attacking the Wuhuan, was enfeoffed as a marquis with 2,000 households. He took Huo Guang's daughter as his wife. In Diji's fourth year he and Huo Guang's sons Yu and others plotted rebellion, and his clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.literal: Ying Ping
cells.idiomatic: Ying Ping

cells.content: 趙充國。以隴西騎士從軍得官，侍中，事武帝。數將兵擊匈奴有功，為護軍都尉，侍中，事昭帝。昭帝崩，議立宣帝，決疑定策，以安宗廟功侯，封二千五百戶。
cells.literal: Zhao Chongguo, as a Longxi cavalryman, followed the army and obtained office as a Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu. He frequently led troops against the Xiongnu and gained merit, becoming Protector Army Colonel and a Palace Attendant under Emperor Zhao. When Emperor Zhao died, he discussed the establishment of Emperor Xuan and decisively settled the plan, earning merit for pacifying the ancestral temple and being enfeoffed as a marquis with 2,500 households.

cells.literal: Yang Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Yang Cheng

cells.content: 田延年。以軍吏事昭帝；發覺上官桀謀反事，後留遲不得封，為大司農。本造廢昌邑王議立宣帝，決疑定策，以安宗廟功侯，二千七百戶。逢昭帝崩，方上事並急，因以盜都內錢三千萬。發覺，自殺，國除。
cells.literal: Tian Yannian served Emperor Zhao as an army official; after uncovering Shangguan Jie's plot to rebel, he was detained and did not immediately receive enfeoffment, though he became Grand Agrarian. He had originally helped draft the plan to depose the King of Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan, and for his merit in settling the doubt over the ancestral temple he was enfeoffed as a marquis with 2,700 households. When Emperor Zhao died and the affairs of state were pressing, he stole 30 million from the capital treasury. Once discovered, he killed himself, and his state was abolished.

cells.literal: Ping Qiu
cells.idiomatic: Ping Qiu

cells.content: 王遷，家在衛。為尚書郎，習刀筆之文。侍中，事昭帝。帝崩，立宣帝，決疑定策，以安宗廟功侯，二千戶。為光祿大夫，秩中二千石。坐受諸侯王金錢財。漏洩中事，誅死，國除。
cells.literal: Wang Qian, whose family was in Wei, served as Attendant in the Masters of Writing and mastered documentary drafting. He became a Palace Attendant and served Emperor Zhao. When the emperor died, he helped establish Emperor Xuan, resolved the uncertainty of the succession, and was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand households for pacifying the ancestral temple. He became Director of the Imperial Household with the rank of middle 2,000-dan. He was convicted of receiving gold and property from various nobles and of leaking palace affairs; he was executed and his state was abolished.

cells.literal: Le Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Le Cheng

cells.content: 霍山。山者，大將軍光兄子也。光未死時上書曰：「臣兄驃騎將軍去病從軍有功，病死，賜謚景桓侯，絕無後，臣光願以所封東武陽邑三千五百戶分與山。」天子許之，拜山為侯。後坐謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Huo Shan. Shan was Grand General Huo Guang's nephew. Before Guang died he memorialized, saying: 'My elder brother the Cavalry General Huo Qubing followed the army and achieved merit; he died of illness and was granted the posthumous title Marquis Jinghuan, but left no heirs. I, Guang, wish to divide three thousand five hundred households of my enfeoffment at Dongwuyang and give them to Shan.' The Son of Heaven approved and appointed Shan as marquis. Later he was convicted of plotting rebellion; his clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.idiomatic: Guan Jun

cells.content: 霍雲。以大將軍兄驃騎將軍適孫為侯。地節三年，天子下詔書曰「驃騎將軍去病擊匈奴有功，封為冠軍侯。薨卒，子侯代立，病死無後。春秋之義，善善及子孫，其以邑三千戶封雲為冠軍侯。」後坐謀反，族滅，國除。
cells.literal: Huo Yun. Yun was enfeoffed as marquis as the legitimate grandson of the Grand General's elder brother, the Cavalry General. In Diji 3 the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: 'The Cavalry General Huo Qubing attacked the Xiongnu and achieved merit and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun. He died, and his son the marquis succeeded him; he died of illness without heirs. The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the reward for goodness extends to descendants; therefore let Yun be enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun with a fief of three thousand households.' Later he was convicted of plotting rebellion; his clan was exterminated, and the state was abolished.

cells.literal: Ping En
cells.idiomatic: Ping En

cells.content: 許廣漢，家昌邑。坐事下蠶室，獨有一女，嫁之。宣帝未立時，素與廣漢出入相通，卜相者言當大貴，以故廣漢施恩甚厚。地節三年，封為侯，邑三千戶。病死無後，國除。
cells.literal: Xu Guanghan, whose family was in Changyi, was convicted of an offense and sent to the silkworm room; he had only one daughter, whom the emperor married. Before Emperor Xuan was established, he and Guanghan had long been close companions; diviners said Guanghan would become very noble, and for that reason Guanghan showed him great favor. In Diji 3 he was enfeoffed as marquis with a fief of three thousand households. He died of illness without heirs, and the state was abolished.

cells.idiomatic: Chang Shui

cells.content: 田廣明。故郎，為司馬，稍遷至南郡都尉、淮陽太守、鴻臚、左馮翊。昭帝崩，議廢昌邑王，立宣帝，決疑定策，以安宗廟。本始三年，封為侯，邑二千三百戶。為御史大夫。後為祁連將軍，擊匈奴，軍不至質，當死，自殺，國除。
cells.literal: Tian Guangming. Formerly a Palace Attendant, he became a major and was gradually promoted to Colonel of Nanjun, Grand Administrator of Huaiyang, Grand Honglu, and Left Governor of Fengyi. When Emperor Zhao died, he took part in the deliberation to depose the King of Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan, resolved the uncertainty of the succession, and pacified the ancestral temple. In Benshi 3 he was enfeoffed as marquis with a fief of two thousand three hundred households. He became Grand Minister of Justice. Later, as General of Qilian, he attacked the Xiongnu; his army failed to reach the rendezvous, he was liable for death, committed suicide, and the state was abolished.

cells.idiomatic: Gao Ping

cells.content: 魏相，家在濟陰。少學易，為府卒史，以賢良舉為茂陵令，遷河南太守。坐賊殺不辜，繫獄，當死，會赦，免為庶人。有詔守茂陵令，為楊州刺史，入為諫議大夫，復為河南太守，遷為大司農、御史大夫。地節三年，譖毀韋賢，代為丞相，封千五百戶。病死，長子賓代立，坐祠廟失侯。
cells.literal: Wei Xiang, whose family was in Jiyin, studied the Changes in his youth, became a headquarters clerk, and was selected as Maoling magistrate on the worthy-and-good recommendation. He was promoted to Grand Administrator of Henan. He was convicted of banditry and killing the innocent, imprisoned, and liable for death; an amnesty came and he was dismissed as a commoner. By edict he was ordered to hold the post of Maoling magistrate, became Inspector of Yangzhou, entered office as Grand Master of Remonstrance, again became Grand Administrator of Henan, and was promoted to Grand Agrarian and Grand Minister of Justice. In Diji 3 he slandered Wei Xian, replaced him as Chancellor, and was enfeoffed with one thousand five hundred households. He died of illness; his eldest son Bin succeeded, was convicted over a temple sacrifice, and lost the marquisate.

cells.literal: Bo Wang
cells.idiomatic: Bo Wang

cells.content: 許中翁。以平恩侯許廣漢弟封為侯，邑二千戶。亦故有私恩，為長樂衛尉。死，子延年代立。
cells.literal: Xu Zhong Weng. With Ping En Marquis Xu Guanghan younger brother enfeoffed as Marquis, fief two thousand households. Also formerly had private favor, became Chang Le Guard Commander. Died, son Yan Nian succeeded.
cells.idiomatic: Xu Zhongweng. As the younger brother of Xu Guanghan, Marquis of Ping'en, he was enfeoffed as marquis with a fief of two thousand households. He had formerly received private favor and became Guard Commander of Changle. When he died, his son Yannian succeeded him.

cells.content: 樂平
cells.literal: Le Ping
cells.idiomatic: Le Ping

cells.content: 許翁孫。以平恩侯許廣漢少弟故為侯，封二千戶。拜為彊弩將軍，擊破西羌，還，更拜為大司馬、光祿勳。亦故有私恩，故得封。嗜酒好色，以早病死。子湯代立。
cells.literal: Xu Weng Sun. With Ping En Marquis Xu Guanghan youngest younger brother therefore as Marquis, enfeoffed two thousand households. Appointed Strong Crossbow General, attacked broke Western Qiang, returned, again appointed Grand Marshal, Guanglu Xun. Also formerly had private favor, therefore obtained enfeoffment. Addicted to wine fond of sex, died early of illness. Son Tang succeeded.
cells.idiomatic: Xu Wengsun. As the youngest younger brother of Xu Guanghan, Marquis of Ping'en, he was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand households. He was appointed Strong Crossbow General, attacked and defeated the Western Qiang, returned, and was then appointed Grand Marshal and Guanglu Xun. He, too, had formerly received private favor and therefore obtained enfeoffment. Addicted to wine and fond of sex, he died early of illness. His son Tang succeeded him.

cells.content: 將陵
cells.literal: Jiang Ling
cells.idiomatic: Jiang Ling

cells.content: 史子回。以宣帝大母家封為侯，二千六百戶，與平臺侯昆弟行也。子回妻宜君，故成王孫，嫉妒，絞殺侍婢四十餘人，盜斷婦人初產子臂膝以為媚道。為人所上書言，論棄市。子回以外家故，不失侯。
cells.literal: Shi Zihui. He was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand six hundred households on account of Emperor Xuan's great-grandmother's family, ranking with his brother the Marquis of Pingtai. Zihui's wife Yijun, a former descendant of King Cheng of Chu, was jealous; she strangled more than forty serving maids and stole the arms and knees of a woman's newborn child for sorcery. Someone memorialized about this, and she was sentenced to execution in the marketplace. Zihui, because of his maternal kin, did not lose his marquisate.

cells.idiomatic: Ping Tai

cells.content: 史子叔。以宣帝大母家封為侯，二千五百戶。衛太子時，史氏內一女於太子，嫁一女魯王，今見魯王亦史氏外孫也。外家有親，以故貴，數得賞賜。
cells.literal: Shi Zishu. He was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand five hundred households on account of Emperor Xuan's great-grandmother's family. In the time of Crown Prince Wei, the Shi clan gave one daughter in marriage to the crown prince and married another daughter to the King of Lu; the present King of Lu is also a grandson of the Shi clan on the maternal side. Because his maternal kin had close ties, he was ennobled and frequently received rewards and bestowals.

cells.literal: Shi Zichang. He was ennobled on account of Emperor Xuan's great-grandmother's family, served as Palace Attendant, and was substantial, heavy, loyal, and trustworthy. For uncovering the Huo clan's plot to rebel he was enfeoffed with three thousand five hundred households.

cells.literal: Bo Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Bo Cheng

cells.content: 張章，父故潁川人，為長安亭長。失官，之北闕上書，寄宿霍氏第舍，臥馬櫪閒，夜聞養馬奴相與語，言諸霍氏子孫欲謀反狀，因上書告反，為侯，封三千戶。
cells.literal: Zhang Zhang, father formerly Yingchuan person, served as Chang'an pavilion chief. Lost office, went to north gate memorialized, lodged in Huo clan residence house, slept in horse stable midst, night heard horse raising slave mutually spoke, spoke various Huo clan sons and grandsons wanted plotting rebellion condition, therefore memorialized reported rebellion, became Marquis, enfeoffed three thousand households.
cells.idiomatic: Zhang Zhang. His father was originally from Yingchuan and served as a pavilion chief in Chang'an. After losing office, Zhang went to the northern palace gate to submit a memorial. He lodged at the Huo clan residence and slept among the horse stalls. At night, he heard the grooms talking with one another about the details of the plot by the Huo sons and grandsons to rebel. He therefore submitted a memorial reporting the rebellion and was made a marquis with three thousand households.

cells.content: 都成。
cells.literal: Du Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Du Cheng

cells.content: 金安上，先故匈奴。以發覺故大將軍霍光子禹等謀反事有功，封侯，二千八百戶。安上者，奉車都尉秺侯從群子。行謹善，退讓以自持，欲傳功德於子孫。
cells.literal: Jin Anshang, formerly a Xiongnu. For uncovering the plot to rebel by the former Grand General Huo Guang's son Yu and others he was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand eight hundred households. Anshang was the son of Colonel of the Carriage Escort Du Hou Congqun. His conduct was careful and good; in retirement he yielded and restrained himself, wishing to transmit merit and virtue to his descendants.
cells.idiomatic: Jin Anshang, formerly a Xiongnu. cells.content: 平通。
cells.literal: Ping Tong
cells.idiomatic: Ping Tong

cells.content: 楊惲，家在華陰，故丞相楊敞少子，任為郎。好士，自喜知人，居眾人中常與人顏色，以故高昌侯董忠引與屏語，言霍氏謀反狀，共發覺告反侯，二千戶，為光祿動。到五鳳四年，作為妖言，大逆罪腰斬，國除。
cells.literal: Yang Yun, family in Huayin, former Chancellor Yang Chang youngest son, appointed Palace Attendant. Loved scholars, self happy knew people, among crowd constantly with people countenance, therefore Gaochang Hou Dong Zhong led with screen spoke, spoke Huo clan plotting rebellion condition, together discovered reported rebellion, Marquis, two thousand households, became Guanglu Xun. Arrived Wufeng fourth year, made demonic words, great rebellion crime waist cut, the state was abolished.
cells.idiomatic: Yang Yun, whose family was in Huayin, was the youngest son of former Chancellor Yang Chang and was appointed Palace Attendant. He loved scholars and prided himself on knowing people; in company he was always open and friendly. For this reason, Marquis Gaochang Dong Zhong drew him aside for a private conversation and told him the details of the Huo clan's plot. Together they exposed and reported the rebellion. Yang Yun was made a marquis with two thousand households and became Superintendent of the Imperial Household. In Wufeng 4, he was convicted of uttering seditious words and gross rebellion, was cut in two at the waist, and his state was abolished.

cells.content: 高昌。
cells.literal: Gao Chang
cells.idiomatic: Gao Chang

cells.content: 董忠，父故潁川陽翟人，以習書詣長安。忠有材力，能騎射，用短兵，給事期門。與張章相習知，章告語忠霍禹謀反狀，忠以語常侍騎郎楊惲，共發覺告反，侯，二千戶。今為梟騎都尉，侍中。坐祠宗廟乘小車，奪百戶。
cells.literal: Dong Zhong, father formerly Yingchuan Yangdi person, with practiced writing went to Chang'an. Zhong had talent strength, could ride shoot, used short weapons, gave service Qimen. With Zhang Zhang mutually practiced knew, Zhang told Zhong Huo Yu plotting rebellion condition, Zhong with spoke to Chang Shi Cavalry Attendant Yang Yun, together discovered reported rebellion, Marquis, two thousand households. Now as Brave Cavalry Colonel, Palace Attendant. Convicted of temple ancestral temple rode small carriage, stripped one hundred households.
cells.idiomatic: Dong Zhong. His father was originally from Yangdi in Yingchuan and went to Chang'an because he was skilled in writing. Zhong had strength and ability: he could ride, shoot, and use short weapons, and he served in the Qimen guard. He was acquainted with Zhang Zhang, and Zhang told him the details of Huo Yu's plot to rebel. Zhong then told the Palace Attendant Cavalryman Yang Yun, and together they exposed and reported the rebellion. He was made a marquis with two thousand households. He now serves as Brave Cavalry Colonel and Palace Attendant. He was convicted of riding a small carriage for the ancestral temple sacrifice and was stripped of one hundred households.

cells.content: 爰戚
cells.literal: Yuan Qi
cells.idiomatic: Yuan Qi

cells.content: 趙成。用發覺楚國事侯，二千三百戶。地節元年，楚王與廣陵王謀反，成發覺反狀，天子推恩廣德義，下詔書曰「無治廣陵王」，廣陵不變更。後復坐祝詛滅國，自殺，國除。今帝復立子為廣陵王。
cells.literal: Zhao Cheng. He was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand three hundred households for uncovering the affair in the state of Chu. In Diji 1 the King of Chu and the King of Guangling plotted rebellion; Cheng discovered the signs of rebellion. The Son of Heaven extended grace to spread virtue and righteousness and issued an edict saying, 'Do not punish the King of Guangling,' and Guangling was not changed. Later he was again convicted of sorcery and curses that exterminated the state; he committed suicide and the state was abolished. The present emperor again established a son as King of Guangling.
cells.idiomatic: Zhao Cheng. He was enfeoffed as marquis with two thousand three hundred households for uncovering the affair in the state of Chu. In Diji 1 the King of Chu and the King of Guangling plotted rebellion; Cheng discovered the signs of rebellion. The Son of Heaven extended grace to spread virtue and righteousness and issued an edict saying, 'Do not punish the King of Guangling,' and Guangling was not changed. Later he was again convicted of sorcery and curses that exterminated the state; he committed suicide and the marquisate was abolished. The present emperor again established a son as King of Guangling.

cells.content: 酇
cells.literal: Zuo
cells.idiomatic: Zuo

cells.content: 地節三年，天子下詔書曰：「朕聞漢之興，相國蕭何功第一，今絕無後，朕甚憐之，其以邑三千戶封蕭何玄孫建世為酇侯」。
cells.literal: In Diji 3 the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: 'I have heard that in Han's rise the Chancellor Xiao He had the foremost merit; now his line is utterly without heirs. I pity this greatly; therefore let his great-grandson Jianshi be enfeoffed as Marquis of Pei with a fief of three thousand households.'
cells.idiomatic: In Diji 3 the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: 'I have heard that in Han's rise the Chancellor Xiao He had the foremost merit; now his line is utterly without heirs. I pity this greatly; therefore let his great-grandson Jianshi be enfeoffed as Marquis of Pei with a fief of three thousand households.'

cells.content: 平昌
cells.literal: Ping Chang
cells.idiomatic: Ping Chang

cells.content: 王長君，家在趙國，常山廣望邑人也。衛太子時，嫁太子家，為太子男史皇孫為配，生子男，絕不聞聲問，行且四十餘歲，至今元康元年中，詔徵，立以為侯，封五千戶。宣帝舅父也。
cells.literal: Wang Changjun, whose family was in Zhao, was a man of Guangwang town in Changshan. In the time of the crown prince he married into the crown prince's household; as the crown prince's male secretary he was matched with Huangsun Zinan and had a son. He lived in obscurity without summons or inquiry for more than forty years, until in the middle of Yuankang 1 he was summoned by edict, established as marquis, and enfeoffed with five thousand households. He was Emperor Xuan's uncle by marriage.
cells.idiomatic: Wang Changjun, whose family was in Zhao, was a man of Guangwang town in Changshan. He lived in obscurity without summons or inquiry for more than forty years, until in the middle of Yuankang 1 he was summoned by edict, established as marquis, and enfeoffed with five thousand households. He was Emperor Xuan's uncle by marriage.

cells.content: 樂昌。
cells.literal: Le Chang
cells.idiomatic: Le Chang

cells.content: 王稚君，家在趙國，常山廣望邑人也。以宣帝舅父外家封為侯，邑五千戶。平昌侯王長君弟也。
cells.literal: Wang Zhijun, whose family was in Zhao, was a man of Guangwang town in Changshan. He was enfeoffed as marquis with a fief of five thousand households on account of Emperor Xuan's uncle by marriage and his maternal kin. He was the younger brother of Pingchang Marquis Wang Changjun.
cells.idiomatic: Wang Zhijun, whose family was in Zhao, was a man of Guangwang town in Changshan. He was enfeoffed as marquis with a fief of five thousand households on account of Emperor Xuan's uncle by marriage and his maternal kin. He was the younger brother of Pingchang Marquis Wang Changjun.

cells.content: 邛成。
cells.literal: Qiong Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Qiong Cheng

cells.content: 王奉光，家在房陵。以女立為宣帝皇后，故封千五百戶。言奉光初生時，夜見光其上，傳聞者以為當貴云。後果以女故為侯。
cells.literal: Wang Feng Guang, family in Fangling. With daughter established as Emperor Xuan Empress, therefore enfeoffed one thousand five hundred households. Spoke Feng Guang first born time, night saw light above it, transmitters believed should be noble. Later indeed with daughter reason became a marquis.
cells.idiomatic: Wang Fengguang, whose family was in Fangling, was enfeoffed with one thousand five hundred households because his daughter was established as Emperor Xuan's empress. It is said that when Fengguang was born, light was seen above him at night, and those who passed on the story believed he would become noble. Later, indeed, he became a marquis because of his daughter.

cells.content: 安遠。
cells.literal: An Yuan
cells.idiomatic: Anyuan

cells.content: 鄭吉，家在會稽。以卒伍起從軍為郎，使護將弛刑士田渠梨。會匈奴單于死，國亂，相攻，日逐王將眾來降漢，先使語吉，吉將吏卒數百人往迎之。眾頗有欲還者，斬殺其渠率，遂與俱入漢。以軍功侯，二千戶。
cells.literal: Zheng Ji, family in Kuaiji. With soldier commoner arose followed army became Palace Attendant, sent protect general released criminal soldiers Tian Quli. Met Xiongnu Chanyu died, state chaotic, mutually attacked, Rizhu king led multitude came to surrender Han, first sent spoke to Ji, Ji led officials soldiers several hundred went welcome. Multitude quite had those wanted return, beheaded killed their leaders, then with altogether entered Han. With military merit Marquis, two thousand households.
cells.idiomatic: Zheng Ji, whose family was in Kuaiji, rose from the ranks as a common soldier and became a Palace Attendant. He was sent to command pardoned convict-soldiers cultivating fields at Quli. When the Xiongnu Chanyu died, the state fell into disorder and factions attacked one another. The Rizhu king led his followers to surrender to Han and first sent word to Ji. Ji led several hundred officials and soldiers to welcome them. When many among the surrendered group wanted to turn back, he beheaded their leaders and then brought the whole group into Han territory. For this military merit he was made a marquis with two thousand households.

cells.content: 博陽。
cells.literal: Bo Yang
cells.idiomatic: Bo Yang

cells.content: 邴吉，家在魯。本以治獄為御史屬，給事大將軍幕府。常施舊恩宣帝，遷為御史大夫，封侯，二千戶。神爵二年，代魏相為丞相。立五歲，病死。子翁孟代立，為將軍，侍中。甘露元年，坐祠宗廟不乘大車而騎至廟門，有罪，奪爵，為關內侯。
cells.literal: Bing Ji, family in Lu. Originally with governing prisons gave service became Judicial Official subordinate, gave service Grand General tent headquarters. Constantly bestowed old favor Emperor Xuan, promoted Grand Minister of Justice, enfeoffed Marquis, two thousand households. Shenjue second year, replaced Wei Xiang as Chancellor. Stood five years, died of illness. Son Weng Meng succeeded, became General, Palace Attendant. Ganlu first year, convicted of ancestral temple sacrifice not rode grand carriage but rode to temple gate, was convicted of a crime, his title was stripped, became Guan Nei Hou.
cells.idiomatic: Bing Ji, whose family was in Lu, originally served in prison administration as a subordinate of the Judicial Official, and later served in the headquarters of the Grand General. Because he had once shown old kindness to Emperor Xuan, he was promoted to Censor Grand Master and enfeoffed as a marquis with two thousand households. In Shenjue 2, he replaced Wei Xiang as Chancellor. He held office for five years and died of illness. His son Wengmeng succeeded him and became a General and Palace Attendant. In Ganlu 1, Wengmeng was convicted because, during an ancestral temple sacrifice, he did not ride in the grand carriage but rode to the temple gate. His title was stripped, and he became a Marquis Within the Pass.

cells.content: 建成。
cells.literal: Jian Cheng
cells.idiomatic: Jian Cheng

cells.content: 黃霸，家在陽夏，以役使徙雲陽。以廉吏為河內守丞，遷為廷尉監，行丞相長史事。坐見知夏侯勝非詔書大不敬罪，久繫獄三歲，從勝學尚書。會赦，以賢良舉為揚州刺史，潁川太守。善化，男女異路，耕者讓畔，賜黃金百斤，秩中二千石。居潁川，入為太子傅，遷御史大夫。五鳳三年，代邴吉為丞相。封千八百戶。
cells.literal: Huang Ba, family in Yangxia, with corvee moved Yunyang. With incorruptible official became Henan governor assistant, promoted Judicial Official supervisor, acted Chancellor long historian affairs. Convicted of seeing knew Xiahou Sheng violated edict great disrespectful crime, long imprisoned three years, followed Sheng studied Shangshu. Met amnesty, with worthy good selected as Yangzhou inspector, Yingchuan grand administrator. Good transformation, male female different paths, plowmen yielded borders, bestowed yellow gold one hundred jin, rank middle two thousand shi. Resided Yingchuan, entered became Crown Prince tutor, promoted Grand Minister of Justice. Wufeng third year, replaced Bing Ji as Chancellor. Enfeoffed one thousand eight hundred households.
cells.idiomatic: Huang Ba, whose family was in Yangxia, was relocated to Yunyang for corvee service. As an incorruptible official, he became assistant to the Governor of Henei, was promoted to Supervisor under the Judicial Official, and acted in the affairs of the Chancellor's Chief Clerk. He was convicted of knowing of Xiahou Sheng's grossly disrespectful violation of an imperial edict and was imprisoned for three years; while in prison he studied the Book of Documents under Xiahou Sheng. After an amnesty, he was recommended as worthy and good, and became Inspector of Yangzhou and then Grand Administrator of Yingchuan. His moral transformation was excellent: men and women used separate roads, farmers yielded boundaries to one another, and he was granted one hundred jin of gold and the rank of fully two thousand bushels. From Yingchuan he entered court as Tutor to the Crown Prince and was promoted to Censor Grand Master. In Wufeng 3, he replaced Bing Ji as Chancellor and was enfeoffed with one thousand eight hundred households.

cells.content: 西平。
cells.literal: Xi Ping
cells.idiomatic: Xi Ping

cells.content: 于定國，家在東海。本以治獄給事為廷尉史，稍遷御史中丞。上書諫昌邑王，遷為光祿大夫，為廷尉。乃師受春秋，變道行化，謀厚愛人。遷為御史大夫，代黃霸為丞相。
cells.literal: Yu Ding Guo, family in Donghai. Originally with governing prisons gave service became Judicial Official historian, gradually promoted Grand Minister of Justice middle captain. Memorialized admonished Changyi king, promoted Guanglu Dafu, became Judicial Official. Then teacher received Spring and Autumn, changed way practiced transformation, planned substantial loved people. Promoted Grand Minister of Justice, replaced Huang Ba as Chancellor.
cells.idiomatic: Yu Dingguo, whose family was in Donghai, originally served in prison administration as a clerk under the Judicial Official. He was gradually promoted to middle commandant under the Commandant of Justice. He submitted a memorial admonishing the King of Changyi, was promoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness, and became Commandant of Justice. He then studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under a teacher, changed his methods, practiced moral transformation, and was honest and loved the people. He was promoted to Censor Grand Master and replaced Huang Ba as Chancellor.

translations.literal: Above are those enfeoffed during Emperor Xiaoxuan's time.
translations.idiomatic: The above lists those enfeoffed during Emperor Xiaoxuan's time.

cells.content: 陽平。
cells.literal: Yangping.
cells.idiomatic: Yangping.

cells.content: 王稚君，家在魏郡。故丞相史。女為太子妃。太子立為帝，女為皇后，故侯，千二百戶。初元以來，方盛貴用事，游宦求官於京師者多得其力，未聞其有知略廣宣於國家也。
cells.literal: Wang Zhijun, whose family was in Wei Commandery. He had formerly been a clerk to the Chancellor. His daughter became Crown Princess; when the Crown Prince was enthroned as emperor, his daughter became empress, and for this reason he was made marquis with twelve hundred households. Since Chuyuan, when he was at the height of favor and influence, many traveling office-seekers in the capital obtained posts through his power, but it has not been heard that he had wisdom or strategy broadly proclaimed in service of the state.
cells.idiomatic: Wang Zhijun, whose family was in Wei Commandery, had formerly served as a clerk to the Chancellor. His daughter became Crown Princess; when the Crown Prince ascended the throne, she became empress, and Wang was therefore made marquis with twelve hundred households. Since Chuyuan, when he stood at the height of favor and influence, many itinerant office-seekers in the capital gained appointments through his power, but I have not heard that he possessed wisdom or strategy of broad benefit to the state.

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Wu, all under Heaven had many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Emperor Wu, the realm was beset by many troubles.

translations.literal: South: campaign against Ou-Yue; north: strike the Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were launched south against Ou-Yue and north against the Chanyu.

translations.literal: Changping gathered troops; the Champion led the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Changping assembled the armies; the Champion Marquis led the advance.

translations.literal: Shuyang bore jade to surrender; Lin Cai broke Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyang came bearing jade in surrender; Lin Cai crushed Yu.

translations.literal: Bolu was the chief minister; Pingjin the great Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: The Bolu Marquis served as chief minister; the Pingjin Marquis was a great Confucian scholar.

translations.literal: Gold seals were worn; purple sashes trailed as they went.
translations.idiomatic: They wore gold seals and purple sashes that trailed in their train.

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhao, meritorious honors and favor were not diminished.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhao, honors and favor for merit remained undiminished.

translations.literal: Alas, the brush ceased; the Chu clan supplemented these.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the Grand Historian laid down his brush; Master Chu supplemented these records.
